clue.text: One indulging Mayfair man over bribe arrangement

parts.note: Mayfair is London's W1 postal district, with the 1 read as the letter I

indicators.note: over tells us the word for the man is turned round

parts.note: Ben is a man's name

indicators.note: arrangement says the letters of bribe are put into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone is indulging a wealthy Mayfair gentleman by fixing up a bribe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'over' turns BEN into NEB; 'arrangement' turns BRIBE into IBBER. Mayfair is a smart district of central London whose postcode is W1.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine-bibber is a heavy drinker, someone who indulges in drink too freely.

clue.text: Greeting which may have a crest at the top?

definitions.text: which may have a crest at the top
definitions.meaning: a sea swell rising to a foaming crest

explanation.surface: A salutation is pictured as wearing a crest on its head, like a coat of arms.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the raised-hand hello; the other is a breaking swell of water, which has a crest.

clue.text: Disreputable old port other people go round

indicators.note: go round says the phrase for other people surrounds the rest

parts.note: other people are not us
Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port

explanation.surface: An old harbour town of ill repute that strangers avoid.
explanation.definitionFit: Notorious means widely known for something bad, so ill-famed or disreputable.

clue.text: Inheritance system upset old boy, leading to coarse language

indicators.note: upset in a down clue turns the abbreviation upside down, reading it upwards

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
rough means coarse
English is a language

explanation.surface: An old boy is upset by crude talk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns OB into BO. 'leading to' just joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Borough-English was an old English custom of inheritance by which the youngest son inherited land.

clue.text: Cooking substance Remus's brother spread round chicken

indicators.note: spread round says one piece is stretched around the other

parts.note: in the Uncle Remus tales the animals are called Brer, meaning brother, as in Brer Rabbit
oil is used in cooking

explanation.surface: Someone smears cooking fat on a chicken, with a nod to the legendary founders of Rome.
explanation.walkthrough: Remus suggests Romulus, his twin in Roman legend; here he is Uncle Remus, narrator of American folk tales in which characters are titled Brer.
explanation.definitionFit: A broiler is a young chicken raised for roasting or grilling.

clue.text: Eastern vessel carrying fish for diplomat's residence

indicators.note: carrying says the vessel holds the fish inside it

parts.note: MY stands for motor yacht, a vessel
a bass is a fish

explanation.surface: An oriental boat with a catch of fish is bound for an ambassador's home.
explanation.definitionFit: An embassy is the official building where an ambassador lives and works.

clue.text: Social worker's maxim about source of problem

indicators.note: about tells us the word for maxim is turned round

parts.note: a saw is an old saying or maxim

indicators.note: source of picks the opening letter of problem

explanation.surface: A council social worker sums up a guiding principle for getting to the root of a case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' turns SAW into WAS. The social worker is not in local government: it is an insect from a colony.
explanation.definitionFit: Wasps live in colonies, so a worker wasp is literally a social insect worker.

clue.text: Share out a levy raised

indicators.note: raised in a down clue means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a toll is a charge or levy

explanation.surface: A tax is hiked and the proceeds divided.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares.

clue.text: Depictions of type of beam used in doorways

indicators.note: used in says the beam word goes inside the doorway word

parts.note: portals are grand doorways
a ray is a beam of light

explanation.surface: An architectural catalogue describes a kind of lintel set into doorframes.
explanation.definitionFit: Portrayals are representations or depictions of someone or something.

clue.text: Teacher takes train, overcoming motorway tension

indicators.note: overcoming in a down clue puts the first word on top of what follows

parts.note: to school is to train
the M1 is Britain's main north-south motorway, with 1 read as I
stress means tension

explanation.surface: A teacher takes the train, beating the motorway stress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes' is a link word. The M1 is the motorway from London to Leeds.
explanation.definitionFit: A schoolmistress is a female teacher in a school.

clue.text: Clergyman about to turn, who may make one cross

indicators.note: turn says the whole assembly is read backwards
about says the clergyman's title goes round the next word

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman

explanation.surface: A vicar about to change direction might annoy someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' and 'turn' work in that order: the container is built first, then read backwards. 'Cross' suggests anger, but it is the X marked on a ballot paper.
explanation.definitionFit: A voter marks an X, a cross, on a ballot paper.

clue.text: New Labour rich giving up hospital round

indicators.note: New says the letters are made anew in a different order
giving up says a letter is dropped from rich

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hospital, as on road signs

explanation.surface: Wealthy New Labour figures abandon hospital funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'giving up' takes H from RICH, leaving RIC; 'New' rearranges LABOUR plus RIC. New Labour was the Blair-era rebranding of Britain's Labour Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Orbicular means circular or spherical, a formal word for round.

clue.text: Expert repairer disturbs owl

parts.note: to trouble someone is to disturb them
an owl hoots, so it is a hooter

explanation.surface: A skilled mechanic is unsettled by an owl.
explanation.definitionFit: A troubleshooter is a specialist who traces and fixes faults.

clue.text: Soldier on stage digesting Rattigan's initial rewording

indicators.note: on in a down clue puts the soldier above the rest

parts.note: a para is a paratrooper, a soldier

indicators.note: digesting says the stage word swallows a letter

parts.note: a phase is a stage

indicators.note: initial picks the first letter of Rattigan's

explanation.surface: A soldier on the theatre stage takes in a Terence Rattigan play and rewrites it.
explanation.walkthrough: Terence Rattigan was an English playwright; 'stage' tempts as theatre but means a phase.
explanation.definitionFit: A paraphrase restates something in other words, a rewording.

clue.text: A different operation initiated in part of plant

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the plant part

parts.note: the anther is the pollen-bearing part of a flower

indicators.note: initiated picks the first letter of operation

explanation.surface: A new surgical procedure is begun on part of a plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Another means a different one, as in try another.

clue.text: Slightly jaundiced male not seeing female in years

indicators.note: in says the trimmed word sits between the two Y's

parts.note: Y is the abbreviation for year, doubled for years

indicators.note: not seeing means the letter for female is left out

parts.note: a fellow is a man

explanation.surface: A man with a yellowish tinge has gone years without seeing a woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not seeing' drops F from FELLOW, leaving ELLOW.
explanation.definitionFit: Jaundice turns the skin yellow, so slightly jaundiced is tinged with that colour.

clue.text: As briefly identified, it goes with old lace

definitions.meaning: As is the chemical symbol, a brief label, for a poisonous element
the poison paired with old lace in the title of a famous comic play

explanation.surface: A garment note says something briefly named is matched with antique lace.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsenic and Old Lace is a 1939 black comedy by Joseph Kesselring, later a Cary Grant film.
explanation.definitionFit: Its symbol in the periodic table is As, and it is the poison in a well-known play title.

clue.text: Endorse opening

definitions.meaning: to sign with the letters of one's name, approving a document
first, as in the first letter of a word

explanation.surface: A signature at the start of proceedings.
explanation.definitionFit: To put your letters on a document approves it; as an adjective it means first or starting.

clue.text: Enrage? It might if one's an evangelical

definitions.text: It might if one's an evangelical
definitions.meaning: the fragrant smoke of high-church ritual might offend a low-church evangelical

explanation.surface: An evangelical is pictured being made furious by church ritual.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition plays on the verb: the noun, perfumed smoke used in Catholic and Anglo-Catholic services, would anger an evangelical.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to make very angry; as a noun it is the scented smoke burned in worship.

clue.text: Ben may overlook these neat creatures

definitions.text: Ben may overlook these neat creatures

parts.words: Ben may overlook these neat creatures
parts.note: a Scottish mountain, a ben, looking down on beasts of a hardy shaggy breed; neat is an old word for cattle

explanation.surface: A man called Ben ignores some tidy animals.
explanation.walkthrough: Ben looks like a name and neat like tidy; a ben is a Scottish peak and neat means oxen.
explanation.definitionFit: These shaggy, long-horned cattle graze the Scottish uplands below the mountains.

clue.text: Instrument from African country requiring no current

indicators.note: requiring no says a letter is left out of the country

parts.note: Gambia is a country in West Africa
I is the symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: An African nation is said to need no electricity supply.
explanation.definitionFit: The gamba, short for viola da gamba, is a bowed string instrument held between the knees.

clue.text: Sort of ox that tosses kids?

indicators.note: tosses says the word for kids is flipped end to end

parts.note: tots are small children

explanation.surface: A kind of bull throws children around.
explanation.definitionFit: A stot is a young bullock, a dialect word for a type of ox.

clue.text: Daughter in Kingsley's island broadcasting acknowledgement

indicators.note: in says the daughter goes inside the novelist's name

parts.note: the novelist Kingsley Amis, with the possessive giving Amis's
on air, so on means broadcasting

explanation.surface: A daughter on Kingsley Amis's island is on the radio making a confession.
explanation.walkthrough: Kingsley Amis was an English comic novelist; his possessive is used letter for letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An admission is a confession or acknowledgement that something is true.

clue.text: Worker once, one holidaying in Cornwall

definitions.meaning: an old word for an ant, a worker insect

explanation.surface: A former employee takes a holiday in the West Country.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-west tip, where locals call visitors by this ant word.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an archaic or dialect name for an ant, and the Cornish term for a summer visitor.

clue.text: Some imbibed a mild milk product

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone sipped a weak beer and a bit of something from the dairy.
explanation.definitionFit: This Dutch cheese is made from cow's milk, so it is a milk product.

clue.text: A special tax intended, say, for evaluation

parts.note: sess, a variant of cess, is an old local tax

indicators.note: say tells us the word for intended is heard, not spelt

parts.note: meant means intended

explanation.surface: A special tax was intended to be used for evaluation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' signals that MEANT is heard, giving MENT.
explanation.definitionFit: An assessment is a judgement or evaluation of something's worth.
